note: Why a personality decision did not run, or ran without personality turning it, in the trait-wiring audit (docs/reports/trait-wiring-2026-10-20.md). One row per decision with a gap; the matrix (scripts/traits/trait-wiring-matrix.ts) joins them. A row is removed when its fix lands.

corruption.offer.why: Runs about 4 times a year (a lobbyist's first meeting with a member on a bill with employer costs, src/core2/modules/interest-groups.ts:372); the yes score never beats corruptionHonestPull 3, so every offer is declined and the trait never turns one.
corruption.offer.fix: Weigh the stake against the official's own money need and calibrate the honesty pull from the honesty-humility effect size.

corruption.take.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
corruption.take.why: Runs only after an offer says yes (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:177); no offer did.

corruption.tell.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
corruption.tell.why: Needs a taken bribe's crime row (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:215); none was written.

justice.report.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
justice.report.why: Needs a crime row from corruption (src/core2/modules/justice.ts:250); ran twice from other crimes.

justice.prosecute.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

justice.plea.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

press.tip.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
press.tip.why: Needs a crime.told event for a taken bribe (src/core2/modules/press.ts:2049).

recalls.organize.why: Only a county or city ordinance taking effect starts one, and only where the state allows recall without grounds (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts:159, :190); most places have no petition recall or require grounds.
recalls.organize.fix: Let a reported scandal or crime start a for-cause recall where the state requires grounds.

recalls.vote.why: Needs a recall on the ballot (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts:380).

ballot-measures.vote.class: runs only on a date outside the year
ballot-measures.vote.why: The earliest measure in data/elections/ballot-measures.json is June 16, 2026; the played year ends January 20, 2026.
ballot-measures.vote.fix: Add odd-year measures or let an ordinance refer a local measure.

voting.turnout.class: runs only on a date outside the year
voting.turnout.why: The played year runs January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026; most places hold no election in 2025, so turnout runs only where a 2025 local or state election exists.
voting.turnout.fix: Seed odd-year local elections where the place holds them; measure in a second year otherwise.

voting.back-incumbent.class: runs only on a date outside the year

voting.exit-poll.class: runs only on a date outside the year

campaigns.answer-poll.why: Needs a campaign that has set aside enough for a poll (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts, pollFund against pollMinimumInterviews); no local campaign in four played places did.
campaigns.answer-poll.fix: Weight calibrated from the adults of a drawn town (campaigns.traits.test.ts); the call-time path runs when a state or federal campaign raises enough.

offices.accept-appointment.why: Runs only when a serving local official dies or moves away and the post fills by appointment (src/core2/modules/offices.ts:1067).
offices.accept-appointment.fix: Add resignation as a vacancy cause.

constituent-cases.handle-case.class: no trigger (staff takes the case first)
constituent-cases.handle-case.why: A staffer's decision is tried first (src/core2/modules/constituent-cases.ts:451), so the official's own read never runs where an official has staff.
constituent-cases.handle-case.fix: Let the official's own lean set what the staffer is told.

conversation.believe-claim.why: Read only when the player's line makes a claim (src/director/conversation.ts:2169).
conversation.believe-claim.fix: Read it where people pass on claims to each other (speech retell, news pass-on).

conversation.reply-reach.why: Read only in a conversation the player opens.
conversation.reply-reach.fix: Player-only by design; covered by the player's conversations.

bring-it-up.blame.why: Read only in a conversation the player opens (src/director/bring-it-up.ts:105).

press.dig.class: runs only on a date outside the year
press.dig.why: Follows an interview answer that contradicts a record (src/core2/modules/press.ts:1753).

estates.will.why: Runs when someone with an estate dies (src/core2/estates.ts:283).

office-day-state.clemency.why: A weekly clemency petition for a governor who is not the player is in review on another branch.

housing.buy-home.why: No study of personality and becoming a homeowner was found, so the weight stays at the general 1 and the fits against an assumed 1.49 between the thirds are kept here: Holualoa, Hawaii 2.05 (341 weighings, 3 buyers, odds ratio 1.68); Peacham, Vermont none reachable (140 weighings, 1 purchase); place key 2371780 0.1 (791 weighings, 16 buyers, odds ratio 11 at weight 1). A renter now weighs the share of the down payment it is short, from none to all of it (homeBuyReasons, src/core2/modules/housing.ts), instead of a log that ran to minus thirty, and buying sits 0.6 below renting before cost, so households that can pay the down payment sit within reach of a lean. Counted renter households do not buy at all yet (pool item world-counted-renters-buy), so this decision has no counted counterpart.
housing.buy-home.fix: A homeownership study with a trait number, and the counted renters' purchase path.

jobs.apply.why: Kanfer et al. 2001 give only the range of correlations across all antecedents of job search behavior (-.15 to .46; the abstract has no per-trait number), so the target is assumed (an odds ratio of 1.49 between the thirds, 1.2 per standard deviation). A seeker's push to apply now eases with the weeks looked (applyNeed, src/core2/modules/jobs.ts), so some applications sit near waiting; the weight fit 0.2, 0.7 and 0.4 in three runs of Holualoa's year (about 1,400 calls each) and 0.4 stands. In a small place (Peacham, 142 calls) nothing turned.
jobs.apply.fix: A study that reports a per-trait size for job search intensity.

drives.respond.why: Personality turned none of 1,471 drive responses in Ely, Nevada at any weight up to 8: the drive's own strength separates the options. No study gives a size (neuroticism and rumination is the direction).
drives.respond.fix: None until the options score closer or a study gives a size; the general trait weight of 1 stands.

business.open-location.why: Owners never open a second location in 282 weighings: the expand score sits 6 to 9 below keeping (baseline -3, room term, src/core2/modules/business.ts:1551), and no study of owners' expansion by personality has a number.
business.open-location.fix: Find a study of owner expansion and calibrate the expand baseline against it.

business.owner-draw.why: No study of owners' draws by personality has a number, so the target is assumed (an odds ratio of 1.49 between the thirds). An owner now weighs the business's cash against a month of everything it pays out, not only payroll (a firm with no payroll had no cushion, so all its cash looked spare and every owner drew), so 40 to 50 percent of weighings sit within a point of keeping. Weight 0.15 fits both drawn towns (Holualoa 221 weighings, odds ratio 1.62; Peacham 198, 1.71).
business.owner-draw.fix: A study that reports owners' withdrawals by trait.

school.attend.why: Children attend 99.95% of school days (10,587 kept weighings, Ely, Nevada); personality turns none below a weight of 1 and at 1 the third least inclined misses at 11 times the odds. Real chronic absence is far higher and follows illness, family and poverty, which the school choice does not read (src/core2/modules/school.ts:149). Poropat 2009 (conscientiousness r 0.19) measures performance, not attendance.
school.attend.fix: Give the school choice the child's illness and the household's circumstances, then calibrate.

life.daily-act.why: Personality turned 14.8% of 29,520 daily-activity picks at the general trait weight of 1. Studies of extraversion and time spent socializing (Mehl et al. 2006) report no extractable coefficient, so the general weight stands.
life.daily-act.fix: Calibrate when a study gives a size for extraversion and social time.

campaigns.volunteer.why: Most adults a campaign reaches share one reason total: no warmth toward the candidate yet, no tie, no family link and no work hours (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts volunteerReason). Where the yes line falls inside that pile, temperament alone sorts them, so one town's odds ratio between the thirds of lean runs from about 1 to over 30 (Red Cliff, Colorado, 424 calls: 34.6 at a one-in-twenty yes share, against Mondak et al.'s 2.41).
campaigns.volunteer.fix: Give the volunteer choice the person's own free time, interest in the race and agreement with the platform, then calibrate the weight.

housing.settle-arrears.class: counted households have no arrears of their own
housing.settle-arrears.why: Runs each month for every full household with rent owed (src/core2/modules/housing.ts, review calls settleArrears and writes a `settlements` row per household and month; 16 rows in Holualoa's year, 11 weighings in Peacham's) and once when a counted household behind on rent is filled in. It does not run monthly for counted households: their rent is paid from a pool shared by place, and the pool repays its group's arrears every month before anything else (src/core2/counted-money.ts, chargeGroups asks rent plus the group's arrears), so there is no moment when a counted household holds cash and chooses between settling and letting it lapse. Households behind on rent seldom hold cash beyond a month's living, so the weighings paid nothing in the drawn years. Willingness is a share, so the general weight of 1 stands with no study.
housing.settle-arrears.fix: Give counted households cash and arrears of their own (stopgap SG-WORLD-housing-counted-rent), then weigh them monthly like the full ones.

jobs.raise-for-opening.why: How much of the affordable raise an owner gives an unfilled seat is a share (open-handedness times what the seat can carry), not a two-way choice, so scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts cannot fit it. Thielmann, Spadaro and Balliet 2020 (Psychological Bulletin 146(1), Table 8) give the nearest size: agreeableness .08 and honesty-humility .09 with what an ultimatum proposer offers (data/research/trait-effect-sizes.json, jobs.raise-for-opening), a lab game with students, so the general weight of 1 stands.
jobs.raise-for-opening.fix: A study of employers' wage offers by trait, or a fit of the share against the correlation of .08.
